the Bajocien carbonate rocks in the studied area were affected by deep-sourced metal-rich fluid circulation in response to continent-wide tectonic and thermal events.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the sphalerite formation in the northeastern Jura Mountains was related to hydrothermal fluids derived from the underlying Mesozoic basement.
the Jura Mountains were affected by a hydrothermal event that occurred at the end of the Middle Jurassic and is related to the opening and spreading of the Tethys Ocean.
the sphalerite formation in the northeastern Jura Mountains is related to hydrothermal activity in the Jurassic and not to the Alpine orogeny.
